questions.question: Which Himalayan range is the northern-most and contains the loftiest peaks?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Himadri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Himadri**, also known as the **Greater Himalayas**, is the northernmost range of the Himalayan mountain system.
 
• It contains the **loftiest peaks**, including the world’s highest peak, **Mount Everest (8,848 meters)**, and several other towering peaks like **K2, Kanchenjunga, Nanga Parbat, and Annapurna.**
 
• This range is characterized by its **permanent snow cover** and is home to some of the largest glaciers, such as the **Siachen Glacier** and the **Gangotri Glacier.**
 
• The Himadri range spans across several countries, including **India, Nepal, Bhutan, Pakistan, and China (Tibet).**
 
• The region is geologically young, formed due to the **collision between the Indian Plate and the Eurasian Plate.**
 
• It is a significant source of major rivers like the **Ganges, Yamuna, Indus, Brahmaputra, and their tributaries.**
 
• The Himadri range plays a crucial role in influencing the **climate and weather** patterns in South Asia by blocking cold winds and trapping the monsoon rains.
 
• The region is sparsely populated due to its **extreme climatic conditions**, high altitude, and rugged terrain.
 
• The Himadri serves as a hotspot for **mountaineering, trekking, and adventure tourism**, attracting enthusiasts from across the globe.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Shiwalik Range**__

 __
 
• The **Shiwalik Range**, also known as the **Outer Himalayas**, is the southernmost range of the Himalayas.
 
• It is characterized by **low-altitude hills** (600-1,200 meters) and is known for its **fragile geology.**
 
• This range is primarily composed of **sedimentary rocks**, making it prone to erosion and landslides.
 
• It serves as a transition zone between the plains of northern India and the mountainous terrain of the Himalayas.
 
 
 
• **Himachal Himalaya**__
 __
 
• The **Himachal Himalaya**, also known as the **Lesser Himalayas**, lies between the Shiwalik and Himadri ranges.
 
• This range includes **medium-altitude peaks** (3,700–4,500 meters) and is rich in vegetation and biodiversity.
 
• It is home to **popular hill stations** like Shimla, Manali, Mussoorie, and Nainital.
 
• The region is known for its **agricultural activities**, particularly the cultivation of apples and other fruits.
 
 
 
• **Purvachal Hills**__
 
 
• The **Purvachal Hills** are located in the northeastern part of India and are not part of the Himalayan system.
 
• They include ranges like the **Patkai, Naga, Khasi, Jaintia, and Mizo Hills.**
 
• This region is characterized by **low-altitude hills** and dense forests, making it rich in **biodiversity.**
 
• The Purvachal Hills are known for their **distinct cultural identity** and indigenous tribal communities.

questions.question: Which of the following is not an 'Avanaddha Vadya'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manjira**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Manjira** is a pair of small hand cymbals, commonly used in Indian devotional and folk music.
 
• Manjira is classified as an **Idiophone** instrument, which produces sound primarily by the vibration of the instrument itself, without the use of strings or membranes.
 
• Unlike Avanaddha Vadya (membranophones), Manjira does not have a stretched membrane that is struck to produce sound.
 
• Avanaddha Vadya refers to percussion instruments like Dhol, Tabla, and Damru, which use a tightly stretched membrane to create sound when struck or played.
 
• Manjira is not categorized as an Avanaddha Vadya because it lacks the defining characteristic of a stretched membrane.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Avanaddha Vadya:**

 
 
• These are percussion instruments that produce sound by striking a stretched membrane.
 
• Examples include Tabla, Dhol, Damru, Mridangam, and Pakhawaj.
 
• They are an integral part of Indian classical and folk music.
 
 
 
• **Idiophones:**
 
 
• Instruments that produce sound by vibrating themselves, without the use of strings or membranes.
 
• Examples include Manjira, Ghungroo, and Jal Tarang.
 
• They are primarily used in folk and devotional music in India.
 
 
 
• **Membranophones vs. Idiophones:**
 
 
• Membranophones (like Tabla) use a stretched membrane for sound production, while Idiophones (like Manjira) rely on the material of the instrument itself.
 
• These classifications are part of the Hornbostel-Sachs system of musical instrument categorization.
 
 
 
• **Manjira in Indian Music:**
 
 
• Manjira is often used in bhajans, kirtans, and traditional folk dances.
 
• Its bright, metallic sound complements vocals and other instruments in devotional settings.

questions.question: What type of shrine is the Neeramankara Temple located in Nemam, Kerala, in India known to be?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Sandhara type**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Neeramankara Temple**, located in **Nemam, Kerala**, is known to be built in the **Sandhara type** of shrine architecture.
 
• The term **Sandhara** refers to a type of temple layout in which the structure is **enclosed by walls** and has a **circumambulatory path** (pradakshina patha) around the sanctum (garbhagriha).
 
• Such temples are designed to allow devotees to perform **pradakshina (circumambulation)** of the deity housed in the sanctum.
 
• This architectural style is commonly found in **Indian temple architecture**, particularly in regions where cultural and religious practices emphasize circumambulation as an integral part of worship.
 
• The **Neeramankara Temple** reflects the traditional **Kerala temple architecture**, with its unique wooden carvings, sloped roofs, and intricate design elements.
 
• The temple is a significant **spiritual and cultural center** in the region, drawing devotees and architecture enthusiasts alike.
 
• Sandhara temples often include additional features such as **mandapas (pillared halls)** and **ornamental gateways**, enhancing the aesthetic and functional aspects of the shrine.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sarvatobhadra type**__

 __
 
• The **Sarvatobhadra** type of temple architecture is characterized by its **symmetry and accessibility from all directions**.
 
• This type of temple often has entrances on all four sides, symbolizing the universal accessibility of the deity housed within.
 
• It is commonly found in **North Indian temple architecture**.
 
• Unlike the Sandhara type, it may or may not have a circumambulatory path.
 
 
 
• **Mandapa type**__
 __
 
• A **Mandapa** is a **pillared hall** or pavilion used for religious purposes, particularly in Hindu temples.
 
• It is typically situated in front of the sanctum and serves as a place for **devotees to gather** and participate in rituals.
 
• While Mandapas are part of temple complexes, they are not a standalone architectural style like Sandhara or Sarvatobhadra.
 
 
 
• **Nirandhara type**__
 
 
• The **Nirandhara** type of temple is characterized by the **absence of a circumambulatory path** around the sanctum.
 
• It focuses solely on the central sanctum and does not include space for devotees to perform pradakshina.
 
• These temples are typically smaller and emphasize **direct worship** of the deity without circumambulation.

questions.question: Who won the 2024 Nobel Peace Prize for their significant contributions to global peace and disarmament efforts?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Nihon Hidankyo**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nihon Hidankyo**, also known as the **Japan Confederation of A- and H-Bomb Sufferers Organizations**, is a prominent organization representing survivors of the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki.
 
• Established in **1956**, Nihon Hidankyo is dedicated to advocating for global **nuclear disarmament** and ensuring the voices of atomic bomb survivors, known as **Hibakusha**, are heard internationally.
 
• The organization works tirelessly to bring awareness to the devastating effects of **nuclear weapons** and promote peace by lobbying governments, participating in international forums, and organizing campaigns.
 
• Nihon Hidankyo has played a critical role in pushing for the adoption of treaties such as the **Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons** (TPNW).
 
• Its efforts have also included documenting the stories of atomic bomb survivors to preserve history and prevent future tragedies.
 
• The organization's work aligns with the objectives of the **Nobel Peace Prize**, which recognizes contributions to peace and disarmament.
 
• By highlighting the human cost of nuclear warfare, Nihon Hidankyo has inspired global action toward a world free of nuclear weapons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Antonio Guterres**__

 __
 
• **Antonio Guterres** is the **Secretary-General of the United Nations**, serving since **2017**.
 
• He is known for advocating for **climate action**, **human rights**, and international peace.
 
• While his efforts have been significant, he did not receive the **2024 Nobel Peace Prize**.
 
 
 
• **Al Gore**__
 __
 
• **Al Gore** is a former **Vice President of the United States** and an environmental activist.
 
• He is well-known for his work on **climate change** and received the **Nobel Peace Prize** in **2007**.
 
• However, he was not associated with the award in **2024**.
 
 
 
• **Greta Thunberg**__
 
 
• **Greta Thunberg** is a young Swedish climate activist who has gained international recognition for her efforts to combat **climate change**.
 
• She has inspired global movements such as **Fridays for Future**, but her focus is primarily on environmental issues rather than nuclear disarmament.
 
• While she has been nominated for the **Nobel Peace Prize** in the past, she did not win the award in **2024**.

questions.question: To which regional language's literature did Girish Karnad contribute most through his works?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kannada**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Girish Karnad, a renowned Indian playwright, predominantly contributed to **Kannada literature**.
 
• His works include celebrated plays such as **"Tughlaq," "Hayavadana,"** and **"Nagamandala,"** which were originally written in Kannada and later translated into multiple languages.
 
• Karnad’s plays, rooted in Indian mythology and history, are recognized for their unique blend of traditional and modern themes, addressing contemporary societal issues.
 
• He was honored with the **Jnanpith Award** in 1998 for his outstanding contribution to Kannada literature and Indian theatre.
 
• His work significantly enriched Kannada literature, making it accessible and appreciated on a global scale.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Girish Karnad’s Legacy:**

 
 
• He was an influential figure in Indian theatre and cinema, contributing as a playwright, actor, and director.
 
• Many of his works are inspired by Indian epics, folklore, and historical events, giving them a universal appeal.
 
• Karnad’s plays were known for their deep philosophical undertones and exploration of human emotions.
 
 
 
• **Kannada Literature:**
 
 
• It is one of the oldest and most significant forms of Indian literature, with a history dating back over a thousand years.
 
• Kannada literature has been enriched by notable writers such as Pampa, Kuvempu, and U. R. Ananthamurthy, along with Girish Karnad.
 
• It encompasses poetry, prose, drama, and folk literature, reflecting the cultural and social heritage of Karnataka.
 
 
 
• **Jnanpith Award:**
 
 
• It is India's highest literary honor, awarded annually by the Bharatiya Jnanpith organization.
 
• The award recognizes exceptional contributions to Indian literature across all officially recognized languages.
 
• Girish Karnad received this prestigious award in 1998 for his outstanding contributions to Kannada literature.
 
 
 
• **Theatre in India:**
 
 
• Theatre has been an integral part of Indian culture, evolving from ancient Sanskrit drama to modern experimental plays.
 
• Playwrights like Girish Karnad have bridged the gap between classical and contemporary theatre traditions in India.
 
• Indian theatre often addresses social, political, and philosophical themes, resonating with diverse audiences.

questions.question: Who among the following was the President of the Board of Control at the time of Charter renewal in 1793 in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Henry Dundas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Henry Dundas served as the President of the Board of Control during the Charter renewal of 1793 in India.
 
• The Board of Control was established under the Pitt's India Act of 1784 to oversee the affairs of the East India Company.
 
• The Charter Act of 1793 extended the East India Company's monopoly on trade and emphasized its governance role in India.
 
• Henry Dundas played a significant role in shaping British policy in India during his tenure.
 
• He was a prominent British statesman and a close ally of Prime Minister William Pitt the Younger.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pitt's India Act (1784):**

 
 
• It established the Board of Control to supervise civil, military, and revenue affairs of the East India Company.
 
• The Act aimed to address administrative inefficiencies and corruption in the company’s governance of India.
 
 
 
• **Charter Act of 1793:**
 
 
• It renewed the East India Company's charter for 20 years.
 
• The act reinforced the company's monopoly on trade and its administrative control over British territories in India.
 
• It provided salaries for the members of the Board of Control from Indian revenues.
 
 
 
• **Henry Dundas:**
 
 
• Dundas was a key figure in British politics, known for his influence in colonial administration.
 
• He held the title of 1st Viscount Melville and was instrumental in shaping British imperial policy.
 
 
 
• **East India Company:**
 
 
• Founded in 1600, it was initially a trading company but later became a governing authority in India.
 
• Its governance practices were subject to British parliamentary oversight after the Pitt's India Act.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a 'Sushira Vadya'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sitar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sushira Vadya** refers to wind instruments that produce sound through the vibration of air.
 
• Examples of Sushira Vadya include instruments such as **Bansuri**, **Pungi**, and **Shehnai**, which require air to generate sound.
 
• The **Sitar** is a string instrument and falls under the category of **Tat Vadya (string instruments)**, not Sushira Vadya.
 
• Sushira Vadya instruments are typically played by blowing air through them, unlike string instruments that are played by plucking or strumming.
 
• This categorization is part of the **Indian classical music system**, which divides musical instruments into four types: Tat (string), Avanaddha (percussion), Sushira (wind), and Ghana (solid instruments).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Musical Instrument Classification:**

 
 
• In Indian classical music, instruments are categorized into four groups based on how sound is produced: **Tat (string), Avanaddha (percussion), Sushira (wind), and Ghana (solid).**
 
• **Tat Vadya:** Instruments like Sitar, Veena, and Guitar produce sound by vibrating strings.
 
• **Sushira Vadya:** Instruments like Flute, Pungi, and Shehnai utilize air to create sound.
 
• **Avanaddha Vadya:** Percussion instruments such as Tabla and Mridangam use stretched membranes.
 
• **Ghana Vadya:** Solid instruments like Manjira and Ghatam produce sound by striking.
 
 
 
• **Sitar:**
 
 
• The Sitar is a popular string instrument in Indian classical music, known for its complex structure and resonant sound.
 
• It has movable frets and is played by plucking the strings with a plectrum.
 
• The Sitar is closely associated with Hindustani classical music and has gained international recognition.
 
 
 
• **Bansuri:**
 
 
• The Bansuri is a traditional Indian bamboo flute, categorized under Sushira Vadya.
 
• It is played by blowing air through one end while covering holes to modify the pitch.
 
 
 
• **Pungi and Shehnai:**
 
 
• The Pungi, also known as Been, is a wind instrument primarily used by snake charmers.
 
• The Shehnai is a classical wind instrument often played during auspicious events in India.

questions.question: Independent dance numbers such as Chali, Ramdani and Jhumura are associated with which of the following dance forms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sattriya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sattriya** is a classical dance form of India, originating from **Assam **and was introduced in the **15th century by the Vaishnavite saint Srimanta Sankardev**.
 
• It combines **music, dance, and drama** and is deeply rooted in Vaishnavism, reflecting devotion to Lord Krishna.
 
• Independent dance numbers such as **Chali, Ramdani, and Jhumura** are integral parts of the Sattriya repertoire.
 
• Sattriya was traditionally performed in **satras (monasteries)** by male monks as part of religious rituals and teachings.
 
• In 2000, Sattriya was recognized as one of the **eight classical dance forms of India** by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Classical Dance Forms of India:**

 
 
• India has eight officially recognized classical dance forms: **Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, Kuchipudi, and Sattriya**.
 
• These dances are characterized by their distinct styles and are deeply rooted in spiritual and cultural traditions.
 
 
 
• **Sattras:**
 
 
• Sattras are Vaishnavite monasteries established by Srimanta Sankardev in Assam.
 
• They served as centers for spiritual learning, art, music, and dance.
 
 
 
• **Key Components of Sattriya:**
 
 
• Sattriya consists of Ankiya Nat (drama), Borgeet (devotional songs), and distinct dance numbers like Chali and Jhumura.
 
• It uses intricate hand gestures (mudras), rhythmic footwork, and expressive facial movements.
 
 
 
• **Recognition by Sangeet Natak Akademi:**
 
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi** officially recognized **Sattriya **as a **classical dance **form in **2000**.
 
• This acknowledgment helped promote and preserve the dance form outside Assam.

questions.question: Samantha Bansil's novel, set in precolonial Philippines, is titled:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Black Salt Queen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Black Salt Queen** is a novel written by **Samantha Bansil**, set in the precolonial Philippines.
 
• The book explores themes of culture, identity, and the myths and traditions of the Filipino people during precolonial times.
 
• The novel delves into the lush landscapes, vibrant history, and rich folklore of the Philippines.
 
• Samantha Bansil skillfully blends storytelling with historical context, highlighting the depth of Filipino heritage before the advent of colonization.
 
• It is celebrated for its vivid imagery, compelling narrative, and authentic representation of precolonial Filipino life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Precolonial Philippines**

 
 
• This period refers to the time before Spanish colonization, which began in **1565**.
 
• Filipinos lived in small, self-sufficient communities called barangays, led by chieftains known as datus.
 
• The society was organized, with a strong emphasis on trade, agriculture, and craftsmanship.
 
• Animism and ancestral worship were prevalent, with rituals and myths deeply influencing daily life.
 
 
 
• **Filipino Mythology**
 
 
• Filipino mythology includes a rich pantheon of gods, spirits, and mythical creatures such as the diwata (fairy-like beings) and aswang (a mythical shapeshifter).
 
• Stories were often passed down orally, forming a key part of cultural identity.
 
• These myths served as a way to explain natural phenomena and teach moral lessons.
 
 
 
• **Representation in Literature**
 
 
• Literature plays a crucial role in preserving and showcasing cultural heritage.
 
• Novels like "Black Salt Queen" highlight the importance of precolonial history and its influence on modern identity.
 
• Such works help bridge the gap between historical narratives and contemporary understanding.
 
 
 
• **Author Samantha Bansil**
 
 
• She is known for her focus on Filipino history, culture, and folklore.
 
• Her writing reflects a deep appreciation for the complexities of Filipino heritage.
 
• Through her works, she aims to shed light on stories that have often been overlooked or forgotten.

questions.question: Which of the following national parks is recognised as the world's only floating national park?

options.text: Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Keibul Lamjao National Park**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Keibul Lamjao National Park is located in the state of **Manipur, India**, on Loktak Lake.
 
• It is **recognized as the world's only floating national park**, as it consists of large masses of floating vegetation known as "phumdis."
 
• The park is the **last natural habitat of the endangered Sangai deer**, also known as the dancing deer (Rucervus eldii eldii).
 
• Keibul Lamjao National Park was **declared a national park in 1977** to protect the unique ecosystem and its wildlife.
 
• The park covers an area of approximately **40 square kilometers**, and the phumdis play a critical role in supporting the ecosystem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phumdis:**

 
 
• Phumdis are floating masses of vegetation, soil, and organic matter at various stages of decomposition, unique to Loktak Lake.
 
• They serve as a critical habitat for wildlife and are an integral part of the ecological balance of Loktak Lake.
 
 
 
• **Sangai Deer:**
 
 
• The Sangai deer is an endangered species endemic to Manipur.
 
• It is culturally significant and is referred to as the state animal of Manipur.
 
• The deer’s unique gait, which resembles dancing, has earned it the nickname "dancing deer."
 
 
 
• **Loktak Lake:**
 
 
• Loktak Lake is the largest freshwater lake in northeast India and is known for its phumdis.
 
• The lake plays a crucial role in the livelihood of the local communities and provides water for hydropower generation, irrigation, and drinking purposes.
 
 
 
• **Conservation Efforts:**
 
 
• The Manipur Forest Department, along with other organizations, is actively working to conserve the habitat of the Sangai deer and the unique ecosystem of Keibul Lamjao National Park.
 
• Efforts include monitoring wildlife, reducing human interference, and raising awareness among local communities.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a 'Ghana Vadya'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mridangam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ghana Vadya** refers to the category of Indian classical musical instruments that produce sound primarily through solid vibrating materials without the need for strings or membranes.
 
• Examples of Ghana Vadya include instruments like **Manjira, Jaltarang, and Khartal**, which create sound through striking, shaking, or other solid resonating methods.
 
• **Mridangam**, on the other hand, is a **Avanaddha Vadya** (percussion instrument) that generates sound through the vibration of stretched membranes.
 
• The Mridangam is a barrel-shaped drum used predominantly in Carnatic and other South Indian classical music.
 
• Thus, **Mridangam** does not belong to the Ghana Vadya category, making it the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ghana Vadya:**

 
 
• Ghana Vadya instruments are also called solid instruments or idiophones.
 
• These instruments are struck, shaken, or scraped to produce sound.
 
• Common examples include cymbals (Manjira), gongs, bells, and xylophones.
 
 
 
• **Avanaddha Vadya:**
 
 
• Avanaddha Vadya, or percussion instruments, produce sound by vibrating stretched membranes.
 
• Examples include Mridangam, Tabla, Dhol, and Pakhawaj.
 
• These instruments are used in various forms of Indian classical and folk music.
 
 
 
• **Mridangam:**
 
 
• Mridangam is a double-headed drum traditionally made of jackwood and leather.
 
• It is played with hands and is an essential instrument in Carnatic music performances.
 
 
 
• **Jaltarang:**
 
 
• Jaltarang is a unique Ghana Vadya that consists of water-filled porcelain bowls of different sizes.
 
• It produces sound by striking the bowls with sticks.

questions.question: Which of the following tree species is an example of deciduous vegetation in India ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sal (Shorea robusta)** is a prominent example of deciduous vegetation found in India, particularly in regions with a tropical moist deciduous climate.
 
• It sheds its leaves seasonally, typically during the dry season, to conserve water and adapt to environmental conditions.
 
• Sal forests are widespread in northern and central India, including states like Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, and parts of the Himalayan foothills.
 
• Known for its durable timber, Sal wood is widely used in construction, furniture making, and railway sleepers.
 
• Sal forests are ecologically significant as they support a variety of wildlife and maintain regional biodiversity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Deciduous Vegetation:**

 
 
• Deciduous trees shed their leaves annually, typically during dry or cold seasons, to reduce water loss through transpiration.
 
• Tropical deciduous forests in India are categorized into moist deciduous and dry deciduous forests based on rainfall patterns.
 
 
 
• **Moist Deciduous Forests:**
 
 
• These forests thrive in areas with annual rainfall between 100-200 cm.
 
• Common tree species include Sal, Teak, Mahua, and Bamboo.
 
 
 
• **Dry Deciduous Forests:**
 
 
• These forests are found in regions with 70-100 cm of rainfall annually.
 
• Common species include Babool, Neem, and Acacia.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Importance of Deciduous Forests:**
 
 
• They act as carbon sinks, mitigating climate change.
 
• They provide habitat for diverse flora and fauna.
 
• They prevent soil erosion and maintain hydrological cycles.

questions.question:
According to the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), India’s

 Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) extends upto __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**200 nautical miles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India's Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) extends up to **200 nautical miles** from the baseline as per the **United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).**
 
• The EEZ allows a coastal nation to exercise **sovereign rights** over natural resources, including energy production from water and wind, within this zone.
 
• UNCLOS, adopted in **1982**, defines the rights and responsibilities of nations regarding their use of the world's oceans.
 
• Within the EEZ, India has exclusive rights to exploit and manage **marine resources, fisheries, and mineral exploration.**
 
• UNCLOS ensures that nations respect each other's EEZ boundaries to maintain international peace and cooperation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Baseline:** The baseline is the low-water line along the coast, from which the 200 nautical miles for the EEZ is measured.
 
• **Territorial Sea:** It extends up to 12 nautical miles from the baseline, where the coastal nation exercises complete sovereignty.
 
• **Contiguous Zone:** It extends from 12 to 24 nautical miles, where a country can enforce laws related to customs, immigration, and pollution.
 
• **High Seas:** Beyond the EEZ lies the high seas, which are international waters not under the jurisdiction of any country.
 
• **UNCLOS Significance:** UNCLOS provides a framework for resolving disputes and ensures equitable sharing of marine resources among nations.

questions.question: Which of the following dance forms represents the love stories of Radha and Krishna?

__
 
• **Raslila** is a traditional dance form that depicts the divine love stories of Lord Krishna and Radha, along with the gopis (cowherd girls).
 
• It originated in the Braj region (Mathura, Vrindavan) of Uttar Pradesh, which is considered the birthplace of Lord Krishna.
 
• The dance is deeply rooted in the **Bhakti movement** and is performed as an act of devotion to Krishna.
 
• Raslila combines elements of classical dance, drama, and devotional music to narrate episodes from the life of Krishna, especially his playful interactions with Radha and the gopis.
 
• It is widely performed during festivals such as **Janmashtami** and Holi, which celebrate Krishna's life and teachings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kalbelia**: A folk dance of Rajasthan performed by the Kalbelia community, known for its snake-like movements and vibrant costumes.
 
• **Giddha**: A traditional Punjabi dance performed by women, characterized by energetic movements and synchronized handclaps, usually during celebrations.
 
• **Matki**: A solo folk dance from Madhya Pradesh where the performer balances an earthen pot on their head, showcasing grace and balance.
 
• The **Bhakti movement**: A spiritual movement that emphasized devotion (bhakti) to a personal god, inspiring art forms like Raslila to express divine love.
 
• Raslila is often accompanied by songs from **Vaishnavite literature**, including verses from the Bhagavata Purana and works of poets like Surdas and Jayadeva.

questions.question: Who among the following wrote the book 'Chhaunk: On Food, Economics and Society'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Abhijit Banerjee**__.

__
 
• **Abhijit Banerjee** is a renowned Indian economist who won the **Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences** in 2019, alongside Esther Duflo and Michael Kremer.
 
• He co-authored the book "**Chhaunk: On Food, Economics and Society**," which explores the intersection of food culture, economy, and societal issues.
 
• Banerjee is a professor of economics at the **Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT)**.
 
• His work focuses on poverty alleviation and development economics, with significant contributions to experimental approaches in understanding economic issues.
 
• Abhijit Banerjee has also co-authored other notable books such as "**Poor Economics**" and "**Good Economics for Hard Times**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Experimental Economics**

 
 
• Abhijit Banerjee's work in experimental economics focuses on randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to test the effectiveness of policies on poverty alleviation.
 
• RCTs provide evidence-based insights into what works and what does not in addressing economic challenges.
 
 
 
• **Food Culture and Economics**
 
 
• Banerjee's book "**Chhaunk**" discusses how food habits are deeply influenced by economic conditions and societal structures.
 
• It provides a unique perspective on how food reflects cultural identity and economic disparities.
 
 
 
• **Global Recognition**
 
 
• Abhijit Banerjee's contributions have earned him international acclaim, including the **Nobel Prize** for his approach to addressing global poverty.
 
• He is considered one of the most influential economists of his time.
 
 
 
• **Collaborative Work**
 
 
• Banerjee frequently collaborates with Esther Duflo, his Nobel co-recipient and spouse, on research and writing projects.
 
• Their joint efforts aim to bridge the gap between economic theory and practical solutions to poverty.

questions.question: Who among the following appointed a superintendent (Shahna-i-Mandi) for the effective implementation of market reforms?

• Alauddin Khilji, the second ruler of the Khilji dynasty, implemented significant economic reforms, including market control measures.

• His reforms aimed to prevent hoarding and ensure the availability of essential commodities at fixed and affordable prices.
 
• The Shahna-i-Mandi was responsible for maintaining control over traders and ensuring compliance with the fixed prices.
 
• Alauddin Khilji's market reforms were a pioneering step in medieval India and were aimed at strengthening the state’s economy and reducing exploitation by traders.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Economic Measures:** These reforms were part of broader measures to strengthen the state’s revenue system and establish a centralized economy.

questions.question: 'Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra' in Ajmer was built in the period of which of the following dynasties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Slave Dynasty**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **'Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra'**, located in **Ajmer, Rajasthan**, is one of the earliest examples of Indo-Islamic architecture in India.
 
• It was constructed during the period of the **Slave Dynasty (1206-1290 AD)**, founded by **Qutb al-Din Aibak**, a prominent ruler of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• The structure was originally a **Sanskrit college**, which was converted into a mosque by Qutb al-Din Aibak in 1199 AD.
 
• The name **'Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra'** (meaning "shed of two and a half days") is derived from a legend that suggests the mosque was built in just two and a half days.
 
• The mosque features a mix of **Hindu, Jain, and Islamic architectural styles**, showcasing the transition of Indian architectural traditions during the period.
 
• It is renowned for its **intricate carvings, floral motifs, and calligraphy**, which reflect the skilled craftsmanship of the era.
 
• The mosque is a significant historical site and is considered an important example of the cultural and architectural synthesis that occurred during the Slave Dynasty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lodhi Dynasty**__

 __
 
• The **Lodhi Dynasty** was the last dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate and existed between **1451 and 1526**.
 
• It was founded by **Bahlul Khan Lodhi** and is known for its contributions to Indo-Islamic architecture, including the **Lodhi Gardens** in Delhi.
 
 
 
• **Tughlaq Dynasty**__
 __
 
• The **Tughlaq Dynasty** ruled from **1320 to 1414** and is known for its architectural innovations, such as the construction of **Tughlaqabad Fort** by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq.
 
• The dynasty also focused on urban planning and created several fortified cities.
 
 
 
• **Khilji Dynasty**__
 
 
• The **Khilji Dynasty** ruled from **1290 to 1320** and was known for its military conquests under rulers like **Alauddin Khilji**.
 
• The dynasty contributed to the development of Indo-Islamic architecture, including the construction of the **Alai Darwaza** at the Qutub Complex.

questions.question: 'The Flying Apsara' painting is a masterpiece in which of the following caves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ajanta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **'The Flying Apsara'** is a famous painting located in the **Ajanta Caves**, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Maharashtra, India.
 
• Ajanta Caves are renowned for their exquisite **Buddhist rock-cut architecture** and paintings depicting Jataka tales and the life of Buddha.
 
• 'The Flying Apsara' painting showcases the **elegance and intricate artistry** of ancient Indian painters, emphasizing movement and grace.
 
• The Ajanta frescoes are painted using the **tempera technique**, combining natural pigments and plant-based adhesives to create enduring artworks.
 
• The caves date back to **2nd century BCE to 6th century CE**, representing one of the finest examples of Indian classical art traditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ajanta Caves:**

 
 
• The Ajanta Caves consist of 30 caves, including monasteries and prayer halls, carved into the rock face of a horseshoe-shaped cliff.
 
• The caves are primarily dedicated to **Buddhism** and were used by monks for meditation and teaching.
 
• They are an important cultural and historical site, preserving ancient Indian art, architecture, and religious practices.
 
 
 
• **Artistic Techniques:**
 
 
• The tempera technique used in Ajanta paintings involves mixing pigments with a binding agent such as gum or egg yolk.
 
• The artists employed natural light in the caves, which filtered through openings, to work on the intricate details.
 
• The paintings depict themes like **Buddhist myths, deities, and daily life activities**, showcasing the harmony between religion and art.
 
 
 
• **Apsaras in Indian Art:**
 
 
• Apsaras are celestial maidens or dancers in Indian mythology, often associated with grace, beauty, and divine energy.
 
• 'The Flying Apsara' painting symbolizes the **dynamic movement and ethereal presence** of these celestial beings.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Status:**
 
 
• The Ajanta Caves were designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in **1983**.
 
• They are recognized for their historical importance and artistic achievement, drawing visitors and scholars from around the world.

questions.question: The Periplus of the Erythraean Sea was written in the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1st century AD**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Periplus of the Erythraean Sea** is a Greco-Roman navigational text written in the **1st century AD**.
 
• It provides detailed information about trade routes, ports, and commodities traded across the **Red Sea, Arabian Sea, and Indian Ocean**.
 
• The text is believed to have been authored by an anonymous Greek merchant or sailor.
 
• It serves as a crucial historical source for understanding maritime trade and cultural exchanges between the Roman Empire, India, East Africa, and Arabian regions.
 
• The document mentions **Muziris**, an important port on the southwestern coast of India, highlighting India's significance in ancient trade networks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Periplus:**

 
 
• A "Periplus" is a type of navigational text used by ancient sailors and traders to describe coastlines, ports, and trade routes.
 
• The term is derived from the Greek word "periplous," meaning "sailing around."
 
 
 
• **Erythraean Sea:**
 
 
• The term "Erythraean Sea" in ancient texts refers to the body of water encompassing the Red Sea, Arabian Sea, and parts of the Indian Ocean.
 
• It was a crucial region for maritime trade connecting Europe, Africa, and Asia.
 
 
 
• **Muziris:**
 
 
• Muziris, located in present-day Kerala, India, was a key port mentioned in the Periplus.
 
• It was famous for exporting spices, pearls, ivory, and textiles to the Roman Empire.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Periplus:**
 
 
• The text offers insights into ancient international trade, cultural exchange, and economic systems.
 
• It highlights the interconnectedness of civilizations during the 1st century AD.

questions.question: Which of these is the westernmost inhabited village in India?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: The famous 'Trimurti' sculpture is present in which of the following caves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Elephanta caves**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 'Trimurti' sculpture is located in the **Elephanta Caves**, a UNESCO World Heritage Site near Mumbai, Maharashtra.
 
• The sculpture depicts the **three faces of Lord Shiva**, representing his roles as the Creator (Brahma), Preserver (Vishnu), and Destroyer (Mahesh).
 
• This colossal statue is carved in relief, measuring approximately **20 feet in height**, and is considered one of the finest examples of ancient Indian rock-cut art.
 
• The Elephanta Caves date back to the **5th–7th century CE**, and the Trimurti is the central figure of the main cave, known as the Great Cave or Cave 1.
 
• The caves are attributed to the **Shaivite faith** and reflect the rich cultural and religious heritage of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Elephanta Caves:**

 
 
• Located on Elephanta Island (Gharapuri Island) in Mumbai Harbour, about 10 km from the Gateway of India.
 
• These caves are divided into two groups: **Hindu caves** (dedicated to Lord Shiva) and **Buddhist caves**.
 
• The island was named "Elephanta" by Portuguese explorers after they found a large stone elephant statue there.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Trimurti:**
 
 
• The Trimurti embodies the concept of the cosmic functions of creation, preservation, and destruction in Hinduism.
 
• The three heads symbolize **Satvik (purity), Rajasik (passion), and Tamasik (destruction)** aspects of existence.
 
 
 
• **Artistic Style:**
 
 
• The caves are an excellent example of **Gupta-era architecture**, showcasing intricate carvings and iconography.
 
• The Trimurti relief is considered a masterpiece of Indian art and is an iconic representation of rock-cut sculpture.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO Recognition:**
 
 
• The Elephanta Caves were designated as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in 1987 for their outstanding universal value.
 
• They are preserved as an important cultural heritage of India.

questions.question: Which dance form represents a mock fight between Durga and Mahishasura?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dandiya Raas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dandiya Raas** is a traditional folk dance form originating from Gujarat, India, and is associated with the festival of Navratri.
 
• It represents a mock fight between the Goddess Durga and the demon Mahishasura, symbolizing the victory of good over evil.
 
• Dancers use colorful sticks called **'dandiyas'** as props, representing the swords of Durga during her battle with Mahishasura.
 
• The dance is performed in a group, with participants forming circles and rhythmically clashing their dandiyas in synchronization with the music.
 
• Dandiya Raas is a vibrant and energetic dance, characterized by its intricate movements and coordination among the dancers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Navratri:** Navratri is a nine-night Hindu festival dedicated to the worship of Goddess Durga in her nine forms. Dandiya Raas is prominently performed during this festival.
 
• **Garba vs. Dandiya:** While Dandiya Raas involves the use of sticks, Garba is a similar dance performed without props, where participants clap hands or perform circular movements.
 
• **Mahishasura:** In Hindu mythology, Mahishasura was a powerful demon who could transform into a buffalo. He was ultimately defeated by Goddess Durga, which is celebrated through Dandiya Raas.
 
• **Cultural Significance:** Dandiya Raas showcases the rich cultural heritage of Gujarat and symbolizes themes of joy, unity, and devotion during festive celebrations.
 
• **Modern Adaptations:** While traditionally performed during Navratri, Dandiya Raas has gained popularity globally and is now performed at cultural events and celebrations across various communities.

questions.question: What kind of architectural style is seen in the shikharas of the Jageshwar temple complexes in Uttarakhand, India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Curvilinear shikharas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Jageshwar temple complexes in Uttarakhand are renowned for their **Nagara-style architecture**, which is characterized by curvilinear shikharas (spires).
 
• Curvilinear shikharas are distinctively tall and tapering structures that rise upwards in a convex curve and are a hallmark of North Indian temple architecture.
 
• Jageshwar temples primarily date back to the 7th to 12th centuries CE, showcasing intricate stone carvings and traditional designs.
 
• The shikharas of these temples often have an amalaka (circular disc-like structure) at the top, symbolizing divine energy and protection.
 
• The temple complex consists of over 100 small and large shrines dedicated to Lord Shiva, reflecting the religious significance of the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nagara Style Architecture:**

 
 
• This style is predominant in northern India and is characterized by curvilinear shikharas and multiple smaller towers surrounding the main temple.
 
• Unlike Dravidian architecture, Nagara temples do not have elaborate gateways (gopurams) and often feature intricate carvings on stone.
 
 
 
• **Amalaka:**
 
 
• The amalaka is a distinctive circular stone disc found atop the shikhara, symbolizing purity and spiritual protection.
 
• It is often surmounted by a kalasha (pot-like structure), adding to the aesthetic and symbolic significance of the temple.
 
 
 
• **Jageshwar Temple Complex:**
 
 
• Located in the Almora district of Uttarakhand, this complex is considered one of the oldest centers of Shaivism in India.
 
• The temples are surrounded by dense deodar forests, contributing to their serene and spiritual ambiance.
 
 
 
• **Historical Importance:**
 
 
• The Jageshwar temples are believed to have been built during the Katyuri and Chand dynasties, showcasing the evolution of temple architecture.
 
• The complex has inscriptions and sculptures that provide insights into religious practices and artistic styles of ancient India.
